programs.name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)
programs.description: Federal food assistance program providing monthly benefits on an EBT card for groceries.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly funds on an EBT card to buy groceries at authorized retailers. Benefits are based on household size and income.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals and families. Income generally must be at or below 130% of the federal poverty level (gross) and 100% net.
how_to_apply: Apply at your local DSS/SNAP office or online through your state's benefits portal
documents_needed: Social Security numbers for household members

programs.name: Women, Infants, and Children
programs.description: Nutrition program for pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5.
programs.what_it_does: Provides supplemental foods, nutrition education, and referrals for pregnant/postpartum women, infants, and children under 5.
programs.who_qualifies: Pregnant or postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 at nutritional risk. Income at or below 185% FPL.
how_to_apply: Find a WIC office at wicprograms.org
documents_needed: Proof of pregnancy or child's age

programs.name: National School Lunch Program
programs.description: Free and reduced-price lunches for K-12 students from low-income families.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free or reduced-price lunches to eligible K-12 students during the school year.
programs.who_qualifies: K-12 students. Free meals for families at or below 130% FPL; reduced-price for 130-185% FPL.
how_to_apply: Apply through your child's school district
Complete the free/reduced meal application form
documents_needed: Proof of income or SNAP/TANF case number

programs.name: School Breakfast Program
programs.description: Free and reduced-price breakfasts for K-12 students.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free or reduced-price breakfasts to eligible K-12 students.
programs.who_qualifies: K-12 students from low-income families. Same income thresholds as school lunch.
how_to_apply: Apply through your child's school district

programs.name: Summer Food Service Program
programs.description: Free meals for children 18 and under during summer months when school is out.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free meals to children 18 and under at approved summer sites when school meals are unavailable.
programs.who_qualifies: Children 18 and under in areas with high concentrations of low-income families.
how_to_apply: Find a summer meal site at fns.usda.gov/summerfoodrocks
No application needed — just show up at a site

programs.name: The Emergency Food Assistance Program
programs.description: USDA commodities distributed through local food banks to low-income households.
programs.what_it_does: Provides USDA commodity foods to low-income households through local food banks and pantries.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income households. Eligibility varies by state but generally at or below 185% FPL.
how_to_apply: Find a food bank at feedingamerica.org

programs.name: Child and Adult Care Food Program
programs.description: Meals and snacks for children in day care and adults in adult day care facilities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides reimbursement for nutritious meals served in child care centers, family day care homes, and adult day care centers.
programs.who_qualifies: Children in day care, adults in adult day care facilities. Income-based for family day care homes.
how_to_apply: Enroll through your child care or adult day care provider

programs.name: Commodity Supplemental Food Program
programs.description: Monthly food packages for low-income seniors 60 and older.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly food packages of USDA commodities to low-income seniors 60 and older.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income seniors 60 and older. Income at or below 130% FPL.
how_to_apply: Contact your local CSFP distribution site or food bank

programs.name: Feeding America Network
programs.description: Nationwide network of 200+ food banks and 60,000 food pantries serving communities in need.
programs.what_it_does: Connects people to their nearest food bank or pantry. No documentation required — just show up.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in need. No income verification or documentation required at most sites.
documents_needed: No documentation required at most sites

programs.name: St. Vincent de Paul Food Pantry
programs.description: Faith-based food assistance through local parish conferences — no documentation required.
programs.what_it_does: Provides emergency food assistance through local parish conferences. Home visits available for those who cannot travel.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in need. No income verification or documentation required.
how_to_apply: Contact your local SVdP conference or parish

programs.name: Salvation Army Food Assistance
programs.description: Emergency food assistance through local Salvation Army corps — crisis and ongoing support.
programs.what_it_does: Provides emergency food boxes, meals, and ongoing food assistance through local corps community centers.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in emergency or crisis need.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Salvation Army corps
documents_needed: No documentation required for emergency assistance

programs.name: Catholic Charities Food Programs
programs.description: Food assistance through local Catholic Charities agencies — pantries, meals, and emergency food.
programs.what_it_does: Provides food pantry access, community meals, and emergency food assistance through local agencies.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in need. Services are not restricted by religion.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Catholic Charities agency
documents_needed: No documentation required at most sites

programs.name: Meals on Wheels
programs.description: Home-delivered meals for homebound seniors and some disabled adults.
programs.what_it_does: Delivers nutritious meals directly to the homes of seniors who are homebound or unable to prepare meals.
programs.who_qualifies: Homebound seniors 60+. Some programs serve disabled adults. No strict income requirement.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging

programs.name: Senior Farmers Market Nutrition Program
programs.description: Coupons for low-income seniors to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables at farmers markets.
programs.what_it_does: Provides coupons that can be exchanged for fresh fruits, vegetables, honey, and herbs at farmers markets.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income seniors 60 and older. Income at or below 185% FPL.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging

programs.name: Double Up Food Bucks
programs.description: Doubles the value of SNAP benefits when spent at participating farmers markets.
programs.what_it_does: SNAP recipients get matching funds (up to $20/day at most sites) when they spend SNAP dollars at participating farmers markets.
programs.who_qualifies: SNAP recipients shopping at participating farmers markets.
how_to_apply: Use your EBT card at a participating farmers market

programs.name: Community Food Pantries
programs.description: Local food pantries and community fridges — no documentation required.
programs.what_it_does: Free food distribution through local pantries, community fridges, and mutual aid networks. No questions asked.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in need. No income verification or documentation required.
how_to_apply: Visit FoodFinder.us or FindHelp.org to find nearby pantries

programs.name: Mutual Aid Food Networks
programs.description: Community-organized food sharing networks — no eligibility requirements.
programs.what_it_does: Grassroots food sharing through mutual aid networks. Neighbors helping neighbors with no bureaucracy.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in need. No eligibility requirements.
how_to_apply: Search Facebook or Nextdoor for local mutual aid groups

programs.name: SNAP Outreach & Application Assistance
programs.description: Free help applying for SNAP benefits through legal aid and community organizations.
programs.what_it_does: Community organizations and legal aid offices help people apply for SNAP, navigate the process, and appeal denials.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone who may be eligible for SNAP and needs help with the application.
how_to_apply: Contact your local legal aid office or community action agency

programs.name: FoodFinder App
programs.description: Free app and website to find nearby food assistance — pantries, meals, and distributions.
programs.what_it_does: Searchable database of food pantries, community meals, and food distributions near you. Available as an app and website.
how_to_apply: Visit foodfinder.us or download the FoodFinder app

programs.name: LIHEAP Heating Assistance
programs.description: Federal program helping low-income households pay heating bills.
programs.what_it_does: Helps pay heating bills for low-income households. Benefits go directly to the utility company or fuel vendor.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income households. Income generally at or below 150% FPL, varies by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state LIHEAP office or local community action agency

programs.name: LIHEAP Cooling Assistance
programs.description: Federal program helping low-income households pay cooling/air conditioning bills.
programs.what_it_does: Helps pay cooling bills and may provide fans or air conditioners to low-income households.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income households. Income generally at or below 150% FPL, varies by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state LIHEAP office or local community action agency

programs.name: LIHEAP Energy Crisis Intervention
programs.description: Emergency assistance for imminent utility shutoff or fuel depletion.
programs.what_it_does: Provides emergency funds to prevent utility disconnection or address fuel depletion. Faster processing than regular LIHEAP.
programs.who_qualifies: Households facing imminent utility shutoff or fuel depletion.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LIHEAP provider immediately — emergency track

programs.name: Weatherization Assistance Program
programs.description: Free home energy efficiency improvements for low-income households.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free weatherization services — insulation, air sealing, heating system repairs — to reduce energy costs.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income households at or below 200% FPL. Priority for elderly, disabled, and families with children.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state energy office or local community action agency
documents_needed: Proof of homeownership or landlord permission

programs.name: REACH Utility Company Programs
programs.description: Utility company assistance programs for low-income customers — varies by provider.
programs.what_it_does: Many utility companies offer their own assistance programs for low-income customers, including bill credits and payment plans.

programs.name: Arrearage Management Programs
programs.description: Programs to forgive past-due utility balances for low-income customers who maintain payments.
programs.what_it_does: Forgives a portion of past-due utility balance each month the customer makes on-time payments. Available from many investor-owned utilities.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income customers with past-due utility balances.
how_to_apply: Contact your utility company customer service

programs.name: Budget Billing / Equal Payment Plans
programs.description: Spreads annual utility costs into equal monthly payments to avoid seasonal spikes.
programs.what_it_does: Averages your annual utility costs into equal monthly payments so you don't face high bills in winter or summer.
programs.who_qualifies: Any utility customer. No income requirement.
how_to_apply: Contact your utility company to enroll

programs.name: Low Income Rate Discounts
programs.description: State-regulated utility rate discounts for low-income customers (CARE, FERA, Lifeline rate).
programs.what_it_does: Provides discounted utility rates for qualifying low-income customers. Program names vary by state (CARE in CA, FERA, Lifeline rate).
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income utility customers. Income thresholds vary by state and utility.
how_to_apply: Contact your utility company or state PUC
documents_needed: Proof of income or enrollment in qualifying assistance program

programs.name: Seattle City Light Utility Discount Program
programs.description: Utility discount for low-income Seattle City Light customers — up to 60% off electric bills.
programs.what_it_does: Provides up to 60% discount on electric bills for qualifying low-income Seattle residents.
programs.who_qualifies: Seattle City Light customers with income at or below 70% AMI.

programs.name: LADWP EZ-SAVE Program
programs.description: Utility discount for low-income LADWP customers in Los Angeles.
programs.what_it_does: Provides discounted electricity rates for qualifying low-income Los Angeles residents.
how_to_apply: Apply at ladwp.com or call LADWP customer service

programs.name: PG&E REACH Program
programs.description: Emergency energy assistance for low-income PG&E customers in crisis — administered by Salvation Army.
programs.what_it_does: One-time energy assistance for PG&E customers in crisis. Administered by the Salvation Army.
how_to_apply: Contact the Salvation Army in your area

programs.name: Xcel Energy Electric Assistance Program
programs.description: Assistance for low-income Xcel Energy customers in Minnesota, Colorado, and other states.
programs.what_it_does: Provides bill payment assistance and energy efficiency services for qualifying Xcel Energy customers.

programs.name: ComEd CARES Program
programs.description: Assistance for low-income ComEd customers in Illinois — income below 80% AMI.
programs.what_it_does: Provides bill payment assistance for qualifying ComEd customers in Illinois.
programs.who_qualifies: ComEd customers in Illinois with income below 80% AMI.

programs.name: Pepco Customer Relief Fund
programs.description: Emergency utility assistance for Pepco customers in the DC area — administered by Salvation Army.
programs.what_it_does: Provides emergency bill payment assistance for Pepco customers in the DC area facing crisis.
programs.who_qualifies: Pepco customers in DC area in crisis.

programs.name: Tribal Utility Assistance Programs
programs.description: Utility assistance for tribal members on or near reservations.
programs.what_it_does: Tribal governments and BIA provide utility assistance for tribal members, including heating, cooling, and electricity.
programs.who_qualifies: Tribal members on or near reservations.
how_to_apply: Contact your tribal government office or local BIA agency

programs.name: Emergency Utility Assistance (Local)
programs.description: Local emergency utility assistance from community action agencies, churches, and nonprofits.
programs.what_it_does: Local organizations provide emergency funds to prevent utility shutoff. Often one-time assistance.
how_to_apply: Contact your local community action agency or church

programs.name: Dollar Energy Fund
programs.description: Nonprofit utility assistance for low-income customers in PA, OH, and other states.
programs.what_it_does: Provides grants to help low-income utility customers pay their bills. Funded by customer donations and utility companies.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income utility customers in participating states (PA, OH, etc.).

programs.name: NEUAC Network
programs.description: National network connecting people to local energy assistance programs.
programs.what_it_does: The National Energy & Utility Affordability Coalition connects people to local energy assistance resources.

programs.name: Pacific Power / Rocky Mountain Power Low-Income Programs
programs.description: Low-income assistance programs for Pacific Power and Rocky Mountain Power customers.
programs.what_it_does: Provides bill assistance and energy efficiency programs for low-income customers in OR, WA, UT, WY, and ID.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income customers of Pacific Power or Rocky Mountain Power.

programs.name: National Fuel Assistance Program
programs.description: Low-income assistance for National Fuel customers in the Northeast.
programs.what_it_does: Provides bill payment assistance for low-income National Fuel customers.

programs.name: Section 8 / Housing Choice Voucher
programs.description: Federal rental assistance vouchers for low-income families, elderly, and disabled.
programs.what_it_does: Provides rental vouchers that cover the difference between 30% of household income and fair market rent.
programs.who_qualifies: Very low-income families (income below 50% AMI). Priority for extremely low-income (below 30% AMI).
how_to_apply: Apply at your local Public Housing Authority
programs.note: Long waitlists in most areas — apply as early as possible.

programs.name: Public Housing
programs.description: Government-owned affordable housing for low-income families, elderly, and disabled.
programs.what_it_does: Provides affordable rental housing owned and managed by local Public Housing Authorities. Rent is typically 30% of income.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income families, elderly, and disabled individuals. Income below 80% AMI.
how_to_apply: Apply at your local Public Housing Authority

programs.name: HOME Investment Partnerships Program
programs.description: Federal block grants for affordable housing development and rental assistance.
programs.what_it_does: Provides funds to local governments and nonprofits for building, buying, and rehabilitating affordable housing.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income households (60-80% AMI, varies by locality).
how_to_apply: Contact your local government housing department or nonprofit developer

programs.name: Emergency Solutions Grant
programs.description: Federal funding for emergency shelter, homelessness prevention, and rapid re-housing.
programs.what_it_does: Provides funds for emergency shelters, street outreach, homelessness prevention, and rapid re-housing services.
programs.who_qualifies: Individuals and families who are homeless or at risk of homelessness.
how_to_apply: Contact your local ESG grantee (usually city/county government)
documents_needed: Proof of homelessness or risk of homelessness

programs.name: Continuum of Care Programs
programs.description: Federal programs for homeless individuals and families — coordinated entry, shelter, and housing.
programs.what_it_does: Provides coordinated community-based systems for addressing homelessness including outreach, shelter, transitional housing, and permanent supportive housing.
how_to_apply: Contact your local CoC lead agency

programs.name: HUD-VASH
programs.description: Housing vouchers combined with VA case management for homeless veterans.
programs.what_it_does: Combines Section 8 housing vouchers with VA supportive services for homeless veterans.
how_to_apply: Contact your local VA medical center or Public Housing Authority

programs.name: USDA Section 515 Rural Rental Housing
programs.description: Affordable rental housing for low-income rural residents.
programs.what_it_does: Provides affordable rental housing in rural areas through USDA-financed properties.
how_to_apply: Contact your USDA Rural Development state office

programs.name: USDA Section 502 Direct Loan
programs.description: Low-interest home loans for low-income rural homebuyers — no down payment required.
programs.what_it_does: Provides low-interest home loans with no down payment for low- and very low-income rural households.
programs.who_qualifies: Low- and very low-income households in eligible rural areas.
how_to_apply: Apply at your USDA Rural Development state office

programs.name: USDA Section 504 Home Repair
programs.description: Grants and loans for very low-income rural homeowners to repair their homes. Grants for seniors 62+.
programs.what_it_does: Provides loans up to $40,000 and grants up to $10,000 for home repairs. Grants available only to homeowners 62+.
programs.who_qualifies: Very low-income rural homeowners. Grants limited to homeowners 62 and older.
how_to_apply: Apply at your USDA Rural Development state office

programs.name: BIA Housing Improvement Program
programs.description: Housing repair and replacement for tribal members in substandard housing.
programs.what_it_does: Provides grants for housing repairs, renovations, and replacement for eligible tribal members living in substandard housing.
programs.who_qualifies: Tribal members living in substandard housing on or near reservations.
how_to_apply: Contact your local BIA office or tribal housing authority

programs.name: NAHASDA / Indian Housing Block Grant
programs.description: Block grants for affordable housing for Native Americans and Alaska Natives.
programs.what_it_does: Provides block grants to tribes and Tribally Designated Housing Entities for affordable housing activities.
how_to_apply: Contact your local TDHE (Tribally Designated Housing Entity)

programs.name: Section 184 Indian Home Loan Guarantee
programs.description: Home loan guarantee for Native Americans and Alaska Natives — low down payment.
programs.what_it_does: Guarantees home loans for Native Americans and Alaska Natives with low down payments and flexible underwriting.

programs.name: State Rental Assistance Programs
programs.description: State-level rental assistance for low-income renters at risk of eviction (ERAP and similar).
programs.what_it_does: State-funded programs providing rental assistance to prevent eviction. Programs vary by state.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income renters at risk of eviction.
how_to_apply: Contact your state housing authority or call 211

programs.name: Eviction Prevention / Diversion Programs
programs.description: Local programs to prevent eviction through mediation, legal aid, and emergency funds.
programs.what_it_does: Provides mediation, legal assistance, and emergency rental funds to prevent eviction before it happens.
how_to_apply: Contact your local legal aid office

programs.name: Emergency Motel/Hotel Vouchers
programs.description: Emergency motel/hotel vouchers for people in immediate housing crisis.
programs.what_it_does: Provides temporary motel or hotel stays for people who are homeless or in immediate housing crisis.
programs.who_qualifies: People in immediate housing crisis — homeless, fleeing domestic violence, or displaced.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Salvation Army or shelter

programs.name: Emergency & Transitional Shelter Networks
programs.description: Emergency and transitional shelters for people experiencing homelessness or fleeing crisis.
programs.what_it_does: Network of emergency shelters, transitional housing, and safe havens for people who are homeless or fleeing crisis.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone who is unhoused or fleeing crisis.

programs.name: Habitat for Humanity
programs.description: Affordable homeownership and home repair through volunteer-built housing.
programs.what_it_does: Builds and repairs homes for low-income families through volunteer labor and donations. Homeowners pay affordable mortgages.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income homeowners or prospective homeowners willing to partner (sweat equity).
how_to_apply: Contact your local Habitat for Humanity affiliate

programs.name: National Foundation for Credit Counseling
programs.description: Free and low-cost credit counseling and foreclosure prevention assistance.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free or low-cost credit counseling, debt management plans, and foreclosure prevention services.
programs.who_qualifies: Homeowners facing foreclosure or anyone with debt issues.

programs.name: HUD-Approved Housing Counseling
programs.description: Free housing counseling from HUD-certified counselors — buying, renting, foreclosure, reverse mortgages.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free counseling on buying a home, renting, default, foreclosure, and reverse mortgages.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone with housing questions or concerns.

programs.name: Low Income Housing Tax Credit Units
programs.description: Affordable rental units built through the LIHTC tax credit program — income below 60% AMI.
programs.what_it_does: Affordable rental apartments built through tax credits. Rents are set below market rate for qualifying tenants.
how_to_apply: Search for LIHTC properties in your area

programs.name: Permanent Supportive Housing
programs.description: Long-term housing with wraparound services for chronically homeless individuals with disabilities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides permanent housing combined with supportive services for chronically homeless individuals with disabilities.

programs.name: Rapid Re-Housing
programs.description: Short-term rental assistance and services to help recently homeless people quickly return to housing.
programs.what_it_does: Provides short-term rental assistance, case management, and housing search to help people exit homelessness quickly.
how_to_apply: Access through CoC coordinated entry or local shelter

programs.name: Salvation Army Emergency Rent Assistance
programs.description: Emergency rent assistance from the Salvation Army for people in crisis.
programs.what_it_does: Provides one-time emergency rent assistance to prevent eviction or homelessness.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Salvation Army corps
documents_needed: Eviction notice or proof of crisis

programs.name: Catholic Charities Housing Assistance
programs.description: Housing assistance from Catholic Charities — rent help, transitional housing, and case management.
programs.what_it_does: Provides rental assistance, transitional housing, and case management for people in housing crisis.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals and families in housing crisis. Not restricted by religion.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Catholic Charities agency

programs.name: IRHA / Tribal Housing Authorities (Alaska)
programs.description: Tribal housing authorities serving Alaska Native communities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides housing services for Alaska Native tribal members through regional housing authorities.
how_to_apply: Contact your local TDHE or visit tribalhousings.org

programs.name: Medicaid
programs.description: Federal-state health insurance for low-income individuals and families.
programs.what_it_does: Provides comprehensive health coverage including doctor visits, hospital stays, prescriptions, and more.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income individuals and families. Income below 138% FPL in expansion states.
how_to_apply: Apply at your state Medicaid office or Healthcare.gov
documents_needed: Proof of citizenship or immigration status

programs.name: Children's Health Insurance Program
programs.description: Health insurance for children in families that earn too much for Medicaid but can't afford private insurance.
programs.what_it_does: Provides low-cost health coverage for children including doctor visits, dental, vision, and prescriptions.
programs.who_qualifies: Children in families with income above Medicaid limits but below 200-300% FPL (varies by state).
how_to_apply: Apply at your state CHIP office or Healthcare.gov

programs.name: Medicare
programs.description: Federal health insurance for people 65+ and younger people with certain disabilities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides health coverage including hospital (Part A), medical (Part B), Advantage plans (Part C), and prescription drugs (Part D).
programs.who_qualifies: People 65 and older. People under 65 with certain disabilities who have received SSDI for 24 months.
how_to_apply: Enroll at Medicare.gov or your local Social Security office

programs.name: Medicare Savings Programs
programs.description: State programs that help low-income Medicare beneficiaries pay premiums, deductibles, and copays.
programs.what_it_does: Pays Medicare premiums and may cover deductibles and copays for low-income Medicare beneficiaries.
how_to_apply: Apply at your state Medicaid office

programs.name: Extra Help / Low Income Subsidy (Part D)
programs.description: Federal program that helps pay Medicare Part D prescription drug costs.
programs.what_it_does: Pays Part D premiums, deductibles, and copays for low-income Medicare enrollees. Can save up to $5,000/year.
how_to_apply: Apply at SSA.gov or your local Social Security office

programs.name: ACA Marketplace Plans
programs.description: Health insurance marketplace with subsidies for individuals and families.
programs.what_it_does: Provides health insurance plans with premium tax credits and cost-sharing reductions based on income.
programs.who_qualifies: Individuals and families with income 100-400% FPL (subsidies). Anyone can purchase without subsidies.
how_to_apply: Enroll at Healthcare.gov during open enrollment or after a qualifying life event

programs.name: Indian Health Service
programs.description: Federal health services for American Indians and Alaska Natives.
programs.what_it_does: Provides comprehensive health services including medical, dental, and behavioral health for AI/AN individuals.
programs.who_qualifies: American Indians and Alaska Natives who are members of federally recognized tribes.
how_to_apply: Visit your local IHS facility or tribal clinic

programs.name: Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program
programs.description: Federal program providing HIV/AIDS care and treatment for low-income, uninsured people.
programs.what_it_does: Provides medical care, medications, and support services for people living with HIV/AIDS who are low-income or uninsured.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Ryan White grantee

programs.name: Federally Qualified Health Centers
programs.description: Community health centers providing care on a sliding fee scale regardless of ability to pay.
programs.what_it_does: Provides primary care, dental, mental health, and pharmacy services on a sliding fee scale. No one is turned away.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone. Sliding fee scale based on income. No insurance required.
how_to_apply: Find a health center at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov
documents_needed: Proof of income for sliding scale (not required for care)

programs.name: Community Health Centers
programs.description: Local community health centers providing affordable care regardless of insurance or immigration status.
programs.what_it_does: Provides affordable healthcare services including primary care, dental, and behavioral health on a sliding fee scale.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone regardless of insurance or immigration status.
how_to_apply: Find a health center at findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov
documents_needed: Proof of income for sliding scale

programs.name: 340B Drug Pricing Program
programs.description: Discounted outpatient drugs for patients of qualifying health centers and hospitals.
programs.what_it_does: Requires drug manufacturers to provide outpatient drugs at significantly reduced prices to eligible health care organizations.
programs.who_qualifies: Patients of qualifying FQHCs, hospitals, and other covered entities.
how_to_apply: Access through your FQHC or qualifying hospital's pharmacy
documents_needed: Be a patient of a 340B-covered entity

programs.name: Patient Assistance Programs (Pharma)
programs.description: Free or low-cost medications from pharmaceutical manufacturers for uninsured/underinsured patients.
programs.what_it_does: Pharmaceutical companies provide free or reduced-cost medications to patients who cannot afford them.

programs.name: NeedyMeds Database
programs.description: Database of patient assistance programs, discount drug cards, and free/low-cost clinics.
programs.what_it_does: Comprehensive database to find patient assistance programs, discount drug cards, and free or low-cost clinics.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone needing help with medication costs or finding affordable care.
how_to_apply: Download the NeedyMeds drug discount card

programs.name: Partnership for Prescription Assistance
programs.description: Connects uninsured patients with prescription assistance programs.
programs.what_it_does: Helps uninsured and underinsured patients find and access prescription assistance programs.

programs.name: Hospital Charity Care / Financial Assistance
programs.description: Free or reduced-cost hospital care for low-income patients — required by nonprofit hospitals.
programs.what_it_does: Nonprofit hospitals are required to provide financial assistance to patients who cannot pay. Can cover partial or full bills.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income patients. Thresholds vary by hospital but typically 200-400% FPL.
how_to_apply: Contact the hospital's financial counselor or billing department
Ask about financial assistance before or after treatment

programs.name: Hill-Burton Free/Reduced Cost Care
programs.description: Free or reduced-cost care at Hill-Burton obligated facilities.
programs.what_it_does: Certain hospitals and health facilities that received Hill-Burton construction funds must provide free or reduced-cost care.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income patients at Hill-Burton obligated facilities.
how_to_apply: Visit hrsa.gov/hill-burton to find obligated facilities

programs.name: Veterans Health Administration
programs.description: Comprehensive healthcare for eligible veterans through the VA system.
programs.what_it_does: Provides comprehensive healthcare services including primary care, specialty care, mental health, and prescriptions.
programs.who_qualifies: Eligible veterans based on service history and income.
how_to_apply: Enroll at va.gov/health-care or visit your local VA medical center

programs.name: Vet Center Program
programs.description: Readjustment counseling for combat veterans and their families — free and confidential.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free readjustment counseling, outreach, and referral services for combat veterans, their families, and survivors.
programs.who_qualifies: Combat veterans, their families, and survivors of military sexual trauma.
how_to_apply: Find a Vet Center at va.gov/vet-centers or call 1-877-927-8387
documents_needed: Proof of combat service or military sexual trauma

programs.name: State Children's Mental Health Programs
programs.description: State-funded mental health services for children and adolescents.
programs.what_it_does: Provides mental health assessment, treatment, and support services for children with mental health needs.
programs.who_qualifies: Children with mental health needs. Eligibility varies by state.
how_to_apply: Contact your state behavioral health authority

programs.name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
programs.description: Free 24/7 crisis support for anyone in suicidal crisis or emotional distress.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free, confidential support 24/7 for anyone in suicidal crisis or emotional distress. Call, text, or chat.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in crisis. No eligibility requirements.

programs.name: National Alliance on Mental Illness
programs.description: Mental health support, education, and advocacy through local NAMI affiliates.
programs.what_it_does: Provides support groups, education programs, and advocacy for people with mental illness and their families.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone affected by mental illness. Free programs.
how_to_apply: Visit nami.org or contact your local NAMI affiliate

programs.name: SAMHSA Treatment Locator
programs.description: Find substance use and mental health treatment facilities near you.
programs.what_it_does: Searchable database of substance use and mental health treatment facilities across the US.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone seeking substance use or mental health treatment.

programs.name: Community Mental Health Centers
programs.description: State-funded mental health centers providing care on a sliding fee scale.
programs.what_it_does: Provides outpatient mental health services including therapy, medication management, and crisis services on a sliding scale.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone. Sliding fee scale based on income.
documents_needed: Proof of income for sliding scale

programs.name: Dental School Clinics
programs.description: Free or low-cost dental care from dental students supervised by licensed dentists.
programs.what_it_does: Dental schools provide comprehensive dental care at reduced costs. Care is provided by students under faculty supervision.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone willing to be seen by dental students. Significantly reduced fees.
how_to_apply: Contact your local dental school clinic

programs.name: Donated Dental Services
programs.description: Free dental care for elderly, disabled, and medically fragile people who can't afford it.
programs.what_it_does: Connects elderly, disabled, and medically fragile people with volunteer dentists who provide free comprehensive dental care.
programs.who_qualifies: Elderly, disabled, or medically fragile individuals who cannot afford dental care.
documents_needed: Proof of disability or medical condition

programs.name: Vision USA / InfantSEE
programs.description: Free eye exams for low-income adults and free infant eye assessments.
programs.what_it_does: Vision USA provides free eye exams for low-income, uninsured adults. InfantSEE provides free eye assessments for infants.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income, uninsured adults (Vision USA). Infants 6-12 months (InfantSEE).
documents_needed: Proof of income and insurance status

programs.name: CHAMPVA
programs.description: VA health coverage for dependents of totally disabled or deceased veterans.
programs.what_it_does: Provides health coverage for spouses and children of veterans who are permanently and totally disabled or who died from service-connected conditions.
programs.who_qualifies: Dependents of totally disabled or deceased veterans not eligible for TRICARE.
documents_needed: Proof of veteran's disability or death

programs.name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families
programs.description: Federal-state cash assistance for low-income families with children.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly cash assistance to low-income families with children. Also provides job training and support services.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income families with children. Income and asset limits vary by state.
how_to_apply: Apply at your local DHS/DSS office

programs.name: Supplemental Security Income
programs.description: Monthly cash payments for disabled, blind, or elderly individuals with very low income.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly cash payments to help meet basic needs for food, clothing, and shelter.
programs.who_qualifies: Disabled, blind, or 65+ individuals with very low income and limited resources.
how_to_apply: Apply at SSA.gov or your local Social Security office

programs.name: Social Security Disability Insurance
programs.description: Monthly disability benefits for workers who become disabled and have sufficient work history.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly benefits based on your earnings record if you become disabled and can no longer work.
programs.who_qualifies: Workers with sufficient work credits who have become disabled. Must meet SSA's definition of disability.
how_to_apply: Apply at SSA.gov or your local Social Security office

programs.name: Social Security Retirement Benefits
programs.description: Monthly retirement benefits for workers 62 and older based on lifetime earnings.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly retirement income based on your lifetime earnings. Full benefits at full retirement age (66-67).
programs.who_qualifies: Workers 62 and older with sufficient work credits (40 credits / ~10 years of work).
how_to_apply: Apply at SSA.gov or your local Social Security office

programs.name: Social Security Survivors Benefits
programs.description: Monthly benefits for surviving spouses and dependents of deceased workers.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly benefits to surviving spouses, children, and dependent parents of deceased workers.
programs.who_qualifies: Surviving spouses (60+, or 50+ if disabled), children under 18, and dependent parents 62+.
how_to_apply: Apply at SSA.gov or your local Social Security office

programs.name: Unemployment Insurance
programs.description: Weekly cash benefits for workers who lost their jobs through no fault of their own.
programs.what_it_does: Provides temporary weekly cash benefits while you look for new work. Benefits based on prior earnings.
programs.who_qualifies: Workers who lost their jobs involuntarily and have sufficient work history.
how_to_apply: File at your state unemployment office or online

programs.name: Workers' Compensation
programs.description: Benefits for workers injured or made ill on the job — medical care and wage replacement.
programs.what_it_does: Provides medical care and wage replacement benefits for workers who are injured or become ill due to their job.
programs.who_qualifies: Workers injured or made ill on the job.
how_to_apply: File a claim with your state workers' compensation board

programs.name: Earned Income Tax Credit
programs.description: Tax credit for low-to-moderate income workers — can be worth up to $7,430.
programs.what_it_does: Refundable tax credit that can significantly reduce taxes owed or provide a refund. Worth up to $7,430 for families with 3+ children.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-to-moderate income workers. Must have earned income and file a tax return.
how_to_apply: Claim on your federal tax return
Use VITA free tax prep services
documents_needed: W-2 or proof of earned income

programs.name: Child Tax Credit
programs.description: Tax credit for families with children under 17 — up to $2,000 per child.
programs.what_it_does: Provides up to $2,000 per qualifying child under 17. Partially refundable.
programs.who_qualifies: Families with children under 17. Income phase-out begins at $200,000 (single) / $400,000 (married).
how_to_apply: Claim on your federal tax return

programs.name: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance
programs.description: Free tax preparation for low-to-moderate income individuals — helps claim EITC and CTC.
programs.what_it_does: IRS-certified volunteers prepare tax returns for free, helping people claim credits like EITC and CTC.
how_to_apply: Find a VITA site at irs.gov or call 1-800-906-9887

programs.name: AARP Tax-Aide
programs.description: Free tax preparation for taxpayers 50+ and low-to-moderate income individuals.
programs.what_it_does: AARP Foundation provides free tax preparation with a focus on taxpayers 50 and older.
how_to_apply: Visit aarp.org/tax-aide to find a location

programs.name: General Assistance / State Cash Aid
programs.description: State/local cash assistance for very low-income adults without children.
programs.what_it_does: Provides small monthly cash payments to very low-income adults who don't qualify for TANF. Varies widely by state/county.
programs.who_qualifies: Very low-income adults without children. Not available in all states.
how_to_apply: Apply at your local DHS office

programs.name: BIA General Assistance
programs.description: Cash assistance for American Indians and Alaska Natives who are unable to work.
programs.what_it_does: Provides cash assistance to AI/AN individuals who are unable to work and not eligible for other assistance.

programs.name: Emergency Cash Assistance (Charitable)
programs.description: One-time emergency cash from Salvation Army, Catholic Charities, St. Vincent de Paul, and churches.
programs.what_it_does: Provides one-time emergency cash assistance for rent, utilities, food, or other urgent needs.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Salvation Army, Catholic Charities, or SVdP

programs.name: Modest Needs Foundation
programs.description: Grants for near-poverty workers who don't qualify for other programs.
programs.what_it_does: Provides small grants to workers who are just above poverty but facing a financial crisis that could push them into poverty.
programs.who_qualifies: Workers near poverty who don't qualify for other assistance programs.

programs.name: Mutual Aid Emergency Funds
programs.description: Community-organized emergency cash assistance through mutual aid networks.
programs.what_it_does: Grassroots mutual aid networks provide emergency cash assistance. No bureaucracy, no eligibility requirements.
programs.who_qualifies: Anyone in crisis. No eligibility requirements.
how_to_apply: Search local mutual aid networks on social media

programs.name: Disaster Unemployment Assistance
programs.description: Unemployment benefits for workers affected by federally declared disasters.
programs.what_it_does: Provides unemployment benefits to workers who lost jobs due to a federally declared disaster and don't qualify for regular UI.
programs.who_qualifies: Workers affected by a federally declared disaster.
how_to_apply: File at your state unemployment office after a disaster declaration

programs.name: Trade Adjustment Assistance
programs.description: Benefits for workers who lost jobs due to foreign trade — retraining, job search, and relocation.
programs.what_it_does: Provides retraining, job search allowances, relocation allowances, and income support for workers displaced by foreign trade.
programs.who_qualifies: Workers who lost jobs due to increased imports or shifts in production to foreign countries.
how_to_apply: File through your state workforce agency

programs.name: Black Emergency Relief Funds
programs.description: Emergency relief funds specifically supporting Black individuals and communities in crisis.
programs.what_it_does: Community foundations and Black-led organizations providing emergency cash assistance to Black individuals in crisis.
how_to_apply: Contact your local community foundation or Black-led organization

programs.name: Transgender Emergency Fund
programs.description: Emergency financial assistance for transgender individuals in crisis.
programs.what_it_does: Provides emergency cash assistance for transgender individuals facing housing, medical, or other crises.
how_to_apply: Contact your local LGBTQ center or Trans Lifeline

programs.name: Child Care and Development Fund
programs.description: Federal-state child care subsidies for low-income working families.
programs.what_it_does: Helps low-income families pay for child care so parents can work or attend training/education.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income working families with children under 13.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state child care agency

programs.name: Head Start / Early Head Start
programs.description: Free early childhood education for low-income children 0-5 and pregnant women.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free early childhood education, health, nutrition, and parent involvement services.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income children 0-5 and pregnant women. Income at or below 100% FPL.
how_to_apply: Find a Head Start program at eclkc.ohs.acf.hhs.gov

programs.name: Title I Schools
programs.description: Federal funding for schools with high percentages of low-income students.
programs.what_it_does: Provides additional educational resources and support to schools serving high concentrations of low-income students.
programs.who_qualifies: Students in schools with high poverty rates. No individual application needed.

programs.name: Individuals with Disabilities Education Act
programs.description: Free special education and related services for children with disabilities ages 3-21.
programs.what_it_does: Guarantees free appropriate public education (FAPE) for children with disabilities, including individualized education programs (IEPs).
how_to_apply: Contact your school district's special education department

programs.name: Section 504 Accommodations
programs.description: Accommodations for students with disabilities in public schools.
programs.what_it_does: Provides accommodations and modifications for students with disabilities to ensure equal access to education.
programs.who_qualifies: Students with disabilities that substantially limit a major life activity.

programs.name: Pell Grant
programs.description: Federal grant for low-income college students — up to $7,395 per year (no repayment).
programs.what_it_does: Provides need-based grants for low-income undergraduate students. Does not need to be repaid.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income undergraduate students. Amount based on financial need, cost of attendance, and enrollment status.

programs.name: Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant
programs.description: Additional federal grant for college students with exceptional financial need.
programs.what_it_does: Provides additional grant funding for undergraduate students with exceptional financial need. Priority to Pell Grant recipients.
programs.who_qualifies: College students with exceptional financial need.
how_to_apply: Complete the FAFSA — school awards automatically

programs.name: Federal Work-Study
programs.description: Part-time jobs for college students with financial need — often community service oriented.
programs.what_it_does: Provides part-time employment for undergraduate and graduate students with financial need.
how_to_apply: Complete the FAFSA — school awards automatically

programs.name: AmeriCorps Segal Education Award
programs.description: Education award for completing AmeriCorps service — up to $7,395.
programs.what_it_does: AmeriCorps members who complete their service term receive an education award to pay for college or student loans.
programs.who_qualifies: AmeriCorps volunteers who complete their service term.

programs.name: TRIO Programs (Upward Bound)
programs.description: College preparation and support for first-generation, low-income, and disabled students.
programs.what_it_does: Provides academic tutoring, counseling, mentoring, and financial guidance to help students prepare for and succeed in college.
programs.who_qualifies: First-generation college students, low-income students, and students with disabilities.
documents_needed: Proof of first-generation status or disability

programs.name: GEAR UP
programs.description: College readiness program for students in high-need middle and high schools.
programs.what_it_does: Provides early college awareness and preparation activities for students in high-poverty schools.
programs.who_qualifies: Students in high-need middle and high schools.

programs.name: Promise Neighborhoods
programs.description: Comprehensive support for children in high-poverty neighborhoods — cradle to career.
programs.what_it_does: Provides comprehensive support services for children in high-poverty neighborhoods from birth through college and career.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Promise Neighborhood site

programs.name: Summer Youth Employment Programs
programs.description: Summer jobs for youth 14-24 through local workforce development programs.
programs.what_it_does: Provides paid summer employment opportunities for young people, often combined with skills training.
how_to_apply: Contact your local workforce development board

programs.name: Boys & Girls Clubs
programs.description: After-school and summer programs for youth 6-18 — academic support, recreation, and leadership.
programs.what_it_does: Provides safe, positive environments for youth with programs in academic success, healthy lifestyles, and character development.
documents_needed: No documentation required at most clubs

programs.name: Big Brothers Big Sisters
programs.description: One-to-one mentoring for youth 6-18.
programs.what_it_does: Matches youth with adult mentors for one-to-one relationships that support positive development.

programs.name: YouthBuild
programs.description: Job training and education for disconnected youth 16-24 — construction skills and GED.
programs.what_it_does: Provides job training (primarily construction), GED preparation, and leadership development for disconnected youth.
programs.who_qualifies: Disconnected youth 16-24 who have left school.

programs.name: Job Corps
programs.description: Free residential education and job training for youth 16-24.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free education and vocational training at residential centers for eligible young people.

programs.name: Foster Youth Education Support (Chafee/ETV)
programs.description: Education and training vouchers for current and former foster youth.
programs.what_it_does: Provides education and training vouchers up to $5,000/year for current and former foster youth pursuing postsecondary education.
programs.who_qualifies: Current and former foster youth up to age 26.
how_to_apply: Contact your state child welfare agency

programs.name: 529 / ABLE Savings Accounts
programs.description: Tax-advantaged savings for education (529) and disability (ABLE) expenses.
programs.what_it_does: 529 plans save for education expenses tax-free. ABLE accounts allow disabled individuals to save without losing benefits.
programs.who_qualifies: 529: Anyone saving for education. ABLE: Individuals with disabilities with onset before age 26.
how_to_apply: Open through your state's 529 or ABLE program website

programs.name: VA Disability Compensation
programs.description: Monthly tax-free payments for veterans with service-connected disabilities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly tax-free compensation for disabilities that were caused or made worse by military service.
how_to_apply: Apply at VA.gov or through a VSO

programs.name: VA Pension (Non-Service-Connected)
programs.description: Monthly pension for low-income wartime veterans 65+ or disabled.
programs.what_it_does: Provides monthly income supplement for low-income wartime veterans who are 65+ or permanently disabled.
programs.who_qualifies: Low-income wartime veterans 65+ or permanently and totally disabled.
how_to_apply: Apply at VA.gov or through a VSO

programs.name: Aid & Attendance / Housebound
programs.description: Additional VA pension benefits for veterans who need help with daily activities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides additional monthly payment on top of VA Pension for veterans who need help with daily activities or are housebound.
programs.who_qualifies: VA Pension recipients who need help with daily activities or are housebound.
how_to_apply: Apply at VA.gov or through a VSO
documents_needed: Medical evidence of need for aid

programs.name: GI Bill Education Benefits
programs.description: Education benefits for veterans, servicemembers, and some dependents.
programs.what_it_does: Provides education benefits including tuition, housing allowance, and book stipend for college, vocational training, and more.
programs.who_qualifies: Veterans, active duty servicemembers, and some dependents.

programs.name: Veteran Readiness & Employment (VR&E)
programs.description: Job training and employment services for veterans with service-connected disabilities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides job training, employment accommodations, resume development, and job seeking skills coaching.
programs.who_qualifies: Veterans with service-connected disabilities and employment barriers.

programs.name: Supportive Services for Veteran Families
programs.description: Housing assistance for very low-income veteran families at risk of homelessness.
programs.what_it_does: Provides case management, housing counseling, and temporary financial assistance to prevent homelessness.
programs.who_qualifies: Very low-income veteran families at risk of homelessness.
how_to_apply: Contact an SSVF grantee organization in your area

programs.name: VA Home Loan Guarantee
programs.description: Home loans for veterans with no down payment and no PMI required.
programs.what_it_does: Guarantees home loans for veterans with no down payment, no PMI, and competitive interest rates.
programs.who_qualifies: Veterans, active duty servicemembers, and surviving spouses.

programs.name: CHAMPVA
programs.description: Health coverage for dependents of totally disabled or deceased veterans.
programs.what_it_does: Provides health coverage for spouses and children of veterans who are permanently disabled or who died from service-connected conditions.
programs.who_qualifies: Dependents of totally disabled or deceased veterans not eligible for TRICARE.
documents_needed: Proof of veteran's disability or death

programs.name: State Veteran Benefits
programs.description: State-specific benefits for veterans — property tax exemptions, education, employment preference.
programs.what_it_does: Each state offers additional veteran benefits including property tax exemptions, state education benefits, and hiring preferences.
how_to_apply: Contact your state department of veterans affairs

programs.name: Veterans Service Organizations
programs.description: Free assistance from VFW, DAV, American Legion, and AMVETS for VA claims and benefits.
programs.what_it_does: VSOs provide free help filing VA claims, accessing benefits, and connecting with services. Trained service officers assist veterans.
how_to_apply: Contact your local VFW, DAV, American Legion, or AMVETS post

programs.name: Military OneSource
programs.description: Free support for active duty, Guard, Reserve, and families — counseling, financial, legal.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free confidential support including counseling, financial planning, and legal consultations.
programs.who_qualifies: Active duty, National Guard, Reserve, and their families.

programs.name: TAPS (Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors)
programs.description: Support for families of fallen military members — grief counseling, peer support, and resources.
programs.what_it_does: Provides grief counseling, peer support, and resources for families who have lost a military loved one.
documents_needed: No documentation required to access support

programs.name: Fisher House Foundation
programs.description: Free housing for veteran and military families near VA medical centers.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free temporary housing for families of veterans receiving treatment at VA medical centers.
programs.who_qualifies: Families of veterans or military members receiving treatment at VA medical centers.
how_to_apply: Contact the Fisher House at your VA medical center or visit fisherhouse.org

programs.name: Operation Homefront
programs.description: Financial assistance and housing for military families in crisis.
programs.what_it_does: Provides emergency financial assistance, transitional housing, and permanent homes for military families.

programs.name: Area Agency on Aging Programs
programs.description: Local aging services including meals, transportation, caregiver support, and benefits counseling.
programs.what_it_does: Provides a wide range of services for adults 60+ including meals, transportation, legal assistance, and caregiver support.
programs.who_qualifies: Adults 60 and older. No income requirement for most services.
documents_needed: Proof of age for some services

programs.name: Older Americans Act Title III Services
programs.description: Federal funding for senior services — meals, transportation, legal, health promotion.
programs.what_it_does: Funds a range of services for adults 60+ including congregate meals, home-delivered meals, transportation, and legal assistance.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging

programs.name: State Health Insurance Assistance Program
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from trained volunteers — helps with plan choices, billing, and appeals.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free, unbiased Medicare counseling to help beneficiaries understand their options and resolve issues.

programs.name: NCOA BenefitsCheckUp
programs.description: Free online tool to find benefits for adults 55+ — screens for 2,500+ programs.
programs.what_it_does: Screens adults 55+ for eligibility across 2,500+ federal, state, and local benefit programs.

programs.name: Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly
programs.description: Comprehensive medical and social services for nursing-eligible adults 55+ living in the community.
programs.what_it_does: Provides all-inclusive care including medical, social, and long-term care services to help people stay in their communities.
programs.who_qualifies: Adults 55+ who are certified as needing nursing home-level care but can live safely in the community.

programs.name: Long-Term Care Ombudsman
programs.description: Advocates for residents of nursing homes and assisted living facilities.
programs.what_it_does: Investigates complaints, advocates for residents' rights, and provides information about long-term care facilities.
programs.who_qualifies: Residents of nursing homes and assisted living facilities, and their families.
how_to_apply: Contact your state LTC Ombudsman program
documents_needed: No documentation required to file a complaint

programs.name: Senior Legal Aid Services
programs.description: Free legal assistance for low-income seniors — wills, benefits, housing, abuse.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free legal services for low-income seniors including help with wills, benefits, housing, and elder abuse cases.
how_to_apply: Contact your local legal aid or state bar senior program

programs.name: Senior Community Service Employment Program
programs.description: Job training and part-time community service employment for low-income adults 55+.
programs.what_it_does: Provides part-time community service positions and job training for low-income adults 55+ to help them re-enter the workforce.

programs.name: Retired and Senior Volunteer Program
programs.description: Volunteer opportunities for adults 55+ — meaningful community service.
programs.what_it_does: Connects adults 55+ with volunteer opportunities in their communities.

programs.name: National Family Caregiver Support Program
programs.description: Support services for family caregivers of adults 60+ — respite, counseling, training.
programs.what_it_does: Provides respite care, counseling, support groups, training, and supplemental services for family caregivers.
programs.who_qualifies: Family caregivers of adults 60+. Grandparents raising grandchildren 55+.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging

programs.name: Adult Protective Services
programs.description: Investigates and responds to reports of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of vulnerable adults.
programs.what_it_does: Investigates reports of abuse, neglect, self-neglect, and financial exploitation of adults 18+ (or 60+ depending on state).
programs.who_qualifies: Abused, neglected, or exploited adults. Anyone can report.

programs.name: Eldercare Locator
programs.description: National service connecting older adults and caregivers to local aging resources.
programs.what_it_does: Connects older adults and caregivers to local Area Agencies on Aging and community services.

programs.name: Social Security Lump-Sum Death Payment
programs.description: One-time $255 payment to surviving spouse or child of a deceased worker.
programs.what_it_does: Provides a one-time lump-sum payment of $255 to the surviving spouse or eligible child.
programs.who_qualifies: Surviving spouse who was living with the deceased, or eligible child.
how_to_apply: Apply at your local Social Security office
programs.deadlines: Must apply within 2 years of death

programs.name: VA Burial Benefits
programs.description: Burial benefits for eligible veterans including burial allowance, headstone, and national cemetery.
programs.what_it_does: Provides burial allowance, headstone/marker, presidential memorial certificate, and burial in a national cemetery.
programs.who_qualifies: Eligible veterans. Burial allowance for service-connected death ($2,000) or non-service-connected ($948).
how_to_apply: Apply at VA.gov or through a funeral home

programs.name: FEMA Funeral Assistance
programs.description: Federal funeral assistance for COVID-19 and disaster-related deaths — up to $9,000 per funeral.
programs.what_it_does: Provides financial assistance for funeral expenses related to COVID-19 or federally declared disasters.
programs.who_qualifies: Individuals who incurred funeral expenses for deaths caused by COVID-19 or federally declared disasters.

programs.name: State Indigent Burial Programs
programs.description: State and county programs covering burial costs for families who cannot afford a funeral.
programs.what_it_does: State and county governments provide funds for burial or cremation when families cannot afford funeral expenses.
programs.who_qualifies: Families who cannot afford funeral expenses. Income thresholds vary by state/county.
how_to_apply: Contact your county social services office or coroner's office

programs.name: Medicaid Funeral Assistance
programs.description: Some states cover funeral costs through Medicaid for eligible recipients.
programs.what_it_does: In some states, Medicaid covers funeral and burial costs for Medicaid recipients or those who were eligible at time of death.
programs.who_qualifies: Medicaid recipients or those eligible at time of death. Varies by state.

programs.name: Nonprofit Funeral Assistance
programs.description: Funeral assistance from nonprofits and faith organizations — Modest Needs, churches, community funds.
programs.what_it_does: Various nonprofits and faith organizations provide funeral assistance including Modest Needs, local churches, and community funds.
programs.who_qualifies: Families who cannot afford funeral expenses.
how_to_apply: Contact local churches or faith organizations

programs.name: ABLE Accounts
programs.description: Tax-advantaged savings accounts for people with disabilities — save without losing benefits.
programs.what_it_does: Allows individuals with disabilities to save up to $100,000 without affecting SSI, Medicaid, or other benefits.
programs.who_qualifies: Individuals with significant disabilities with onset before age 26.
how_to_apply: Open through your state's ABLE program
programs.max_benefit: Save up to $100,000 without affecting benefits

programs.name: Vocational Rehabilitation
programs.description: Job training and employment services for people with disabilities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides job training, education, job placement, and other services to help people with disabilities find and keep employment.
programs.who_qualifies: People with disabilities that result in barriers to employment.

programs.name: Ticket to Work
programs.description: Free employment support for SSDI/SSI recipients who want to work.
programs.what_it_does: Provides free employment support services to help SSDI and SSI recipients find and maintain employment without risking benefits.
programs.who_qualifies: SSDI or SSI recipients who want to work.

programs.name: Medicaid (Disability Track)
programs.description: Health coverage for SSI recipients and low-income individuals with disabilities.
programs.what_it_does: Provides comprehensive health coverage for people with disabilities, including those receiving SSI.
programs.who_qualifies: SSI recipients and low-income individuals with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Apply at your state Medicaid office
